mission_02: Implement the Newton-Raphson method, a powerful root-finding algorithm that uses derivative information to achieve quadratic convergence near the root. The method approximates the function locally by its tangent line and finds where this tangent crosses zero: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n). Newton's method converges much faster than bisection (quadratic vs linear convergence) but requires a good initial guess and the derivative. It can fail if the derivative is zero or if the initial guess is far from the root. The method extends naturally to systems of equations using the Jacobian matrix.
